25.1.m: Now, therefore, we shall explain the arrangements of the sacrificial enclosure.
he makes a mark on the western part, in the third [section] diminished by a sixth part.
Fastening the two ends at the two ends of the east-west axis,
he draws [the cord] toward the south by the mark and makes a sign.
From that sign proceeds reduction or increase.
Or, having repeated the length: an additional fourth and the length is the diagonal cord; the remainder is the transverse measure.

25.1.s: dīrghacaturaśrasyākṣṇayārajjuḥ pārśvamānī tiryaṅmānī ca yatpṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṃ karoti
25.1.d: दीर्घचतुरश्रस्याक्ष्णयारज्जुः पार्श्वमानी तिर्यङ्मानी च यत्पृथग्भूते कुरुतस्तदुभयं करोति
25.1.m: The diagonal cord of a rectangle produces both that which the lateral measure and the transverse measure produce separately.
The laying out is stated by means of knowing these.
The diagonal cord of a square produces an area twice as large; [it is] the producing double of the same.
One should increase the standard measure by its third,
and that [third] by its fourth, diminished by a thirty-fourth of itself.

25.1.s: pramāṇaṃ cārdhena vardhayettasyārdhamasyārdhamardhasya cārdhamabhyantaramudasyeccheṣasyārdhaṃ bāhyataḥ śiṣṭaṃ dviguṇaṃ kṛtvā madhye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti
25.1.d: प्रमाणं चार्धेन वर्धयेत्तस्यार्धमस्यार्धमर्धस्य चार्धमभ्यन्तरमुदस्येच्छेषस्यार्धं बाह्यतः शिष्टं द्विगुणं कृत्वा मध्ये लक्षणं करोति
25.1.m: And one should increase the standard measure by half; one should throw inward half of that, and half of this half, and half of the half; [then] having doubled what remains outside of the half of the remainder, he makes a mark in the middle.
He makes a cord of the length of the standard measure with loops at both ends.

25.1.s: madhyelakṣaṇamardhamadhyayośca pṛṣṭhyāyām̐ rajjumāyamya pāśayorlakṣaṇeṣviti śaṅkūnnihantyupāntyayoḥ pāśau pratimucya madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya nimittaṃ karoti | madhyame pāśau pratimucyoparyupari nimittaṃ madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya śaṅkue nihanti | tasminpāśaṃ pratimucya pūrvasminnitaraṃ madhyamena lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamadgasamāyacchedunmucya pūrvasmādaparasminpratimucya madhyamenaiva lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇām̐ śroṇimāyacchedevamuttarau śrauṇyadgasau
25.1.d: मध्येलक्षणमर्धमध्ययोश्च पृष्ठ्यायाँ रज्जुमायम्य पाशयोर्लक्षणेष्विति शङ्कून्निहन्त्युपान्त्ययोः पाशौ प्रतिमुच्य मध्यमेन लक्षणेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य निमित्तं करोति । मध्यमे पाशौ प्रतिमुच्योपर्युपरि निमित्तं मध्यमेन लक्षणेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य शङ्कुए निहन्ति । तस्मिन्पाशं प्रतिमुच्य पूर्वस्मिन्नितरं मध्यमेन लक्षणेन दक्षिणमद्गसमायच्छेदुन्मुच्य पूर्वस्मादपरस्मिन्प्रतिमुच्य मध्यमेनैव लक्षणेन दक्षिणाँ श्रोणिमायच्छेदेवमुत्तरौ श्रौण्यद्गसौ

25.1.s: athāparaṃ pṛṣṭhyāntayormadhye ca śaṅkūnnihatyārdhe tadviśeṣamabhyasya lakṣaṇaṃ kṛtvā'rdhamāgamayedantyayoḥ pāśau kṛtvā madhyame saviśeṣaṃ pratimucya pūrvasminnitaraṃ lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇamadgasamāyacchedunmucya pūrvasmādaparasminpratimucya lakṣaṇenaiva dakṣiṇām̐ śroṇimāyacchedevamuttarau śroṇyadgasau
25.1.d: अथापरं पृष्ठ्यान्तयोर्मध्ये च शङ्कून्निहत्यार्धे तद्विशेषमभ्यस्य लक्षणं कृत्वाऽर्धमागमयेदन्त्ययोः पाशौ कृत्वा मध्यमे सविशेषं प्रतिमुच्य पूर्वस्मिन्नितरं लक्षणेन दक्षिणमद्गसमायच्छेदुन्मुच्य पूर्वस्मादपरस्मिन्प्रतिमुच्य लक्षणेनैव दक्षिणाँ श्रोणिमायच्छेदेवमुत्तरौ श्रोण्यद्गसौ
25.1.m: Now another [method]: Having driven in pegs at the ends of the east-west axis and in the middle, having added its excess to half, having made a mark, he should introduce half. Having made loops at the two ends, fastening [the cord] with the excess to the middle [peg] and the other to the eastern [peg], he should stretch the southern shoulder [corner] by the mark. Unfastening from the eastern [peg] and fastening to the western [peg], he should stretch the southern buttock [corner] by the mark itself. In the same way the northern buttock and shoulder [corners].
The standard measure is the transverse [side], the producing double is the length; its diagonal cord is the producing triple.
By this the producing one-third is explained; but the division is ninefold.
The combination of two equal squares is stated.
The combination of two squares of different sizes:
With the producing side of the smaller, one should mark off [a strip] from the larger.
The diagonal cord of the marked-off piece combines both.

25.1.s: taduktaṃ caturaśrāccaturaśraṃ nijihīrṣanyāvannijihīrṣettasya karaṇyā vṛddhamullikhedvṛddhasya pārśvamānīmakṣṇayetaratpārśvamupasadgaharet | sā yatra nipatettadapacchindyāt
25.1.d: तदुक्तं चतुरश्राच्चतुरश्रं निजिहीर्षन्यावन्निजिहीर्षेत्तस्य करण्या वृद्धमुल्लिखेद्वृद्धस्य पार्श्वमानीमक्ष्णयेतरत्पार्श्वमुपसद्गहरेत् । सा यत्र निपतेत्तदपच्छिन्द्यात्
25.1.m: It is said: Desiring to subtract a square from a square, by the producing side of as much as he wishes to subtract, he should mark off [a strip] from the larger. He should turn the lateral measure of the marked-off piece diagonally toward the other side; where it falls, he should cut that off.
The drawn-in diagonal cord is the producing quadruple.

25.1.s: chinnā cetarā ca yatpṛthagbhūte kurutastadubhayaṃ karoti
25.1.d: छिन्ना चेतरा च यत्पृथग्भूते कुरुतस्तदुभयं करोति
25.1.m: The cut-off [side] and the other produce together what they produce separately.
The transverse measure is one man's height; the remainder is three.

25.1.s: dīrghacaturaśram̐ samacaturaśraṃ cikīṣardgastiryaṅmā nyā'pacchidya śeṣaṃ vibhajyobhayata upadadhyāt
25.1.d: दीर्घचतुरश्रँ समचतुरश्रं चिकीषर्द्गस्तिर्यङ्मा न्याऽपच्छिद्य शेषं विभज्योभयत उपदध्यात्
25.1.m: Wishing to make a rectangle into a square, having cut off a part by the transverse measure, having divided the remainder, one should place [the two halves] on both sides.
One should fill in the corner piece with an additional [square].

25.1.s: samacaturaśraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ cikīrṣanyāvaccikīrṣettāvatīṃ pārśvamānīṃ kṛtvā yāvadadhikam̐ syāttadyathāparimāṇaṃ vibhajya yathāyogamupadadhyāt
25.1.d: समचतुरश्रं दीर्घचतुरश्रं चिकीर्षन्यावच्चिकीर्षेत्तावतीं पार्श्वमानीं कृत्वा यावदधिकँ स्यात्तद्यथापरिमाणं विभज्य यथायोगमुपदध्यात्
25.1.m: Wishing to make a square into a rectangle, having made the lateral measure as much as one wishes, as much as exceeds, having divided that according to measure, one should place [the parts] as suitable.
Wishing to make a square into a circle:
From the center he should drop [the cord] to a corner.
Having drawn it around toward the side, he should draw the circle with a third of the projecting part.
As much as falls short, that much is added.

25.1.s: maṇḍalaṃ caturaśraṃ cikīrṣanviṣkambhaṃ pañcadaśabhāgānkṛtvā dvāvuddharettrayodaśāvaśiṣyante sā'nityā caturaśram
25.1.d: मण्डलं चतुरश्रं चिकीर्षन्विष्कम्भं पञ्चदशभागान्कृत्वा द्वावुद्धरेत्त्रयोदशावशिष्यन्ते साऽनित्या चतुरश्रम्
25.1.m: Wishing to make a circle into a square, having divided the diameter into fifteen parts, one should remove two; thirteen remain. That gives an approximate square.
A square is prescribed as standard measure by standard measure,
Of whatever measure the cord is, so many squares of that size it produces.
A cord of one and a half men's heights produces two and a quarter.
A cord of two and a half men's heights produces six and a quarter. Now the ultimate rule:
By however much excess one draws [around], one places that on the two sides.
The square which one makes with that [excess] goes at the corner.
By half a standard measure, a quarter measure is prescribed,
because two measures of a half fill a quarter [of the whole unit area].

25.2.m: In the sacrificial enclosure of the fire establishment, it is known [from scripture] regarding the space between the Gārhapatya and the Āhavanīya:

25.2.s: aṣṭāsu prakrameṣu brāhmaṇo'gnimādadhīta | ekādaśasu rājanyaḥ dvādaśasu vaiśyaḥ | caturviṃśatyāmaparimite yāvatā vā cakṣuṣā manyeta tasmānnātidūramādheya iti sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇa śrūyate
25.2.d: अष्टासु प्रक्रमेषु ब्राह्मणोऽग्निमादधीत । एकादशसु राजन्यः द्वादशसु वैश्यः । चतुर्विंशत्यामपरिमिते यावता वा चक्षुषा मन्येत तस्मान्नातिदूरमाधेय इति सर्वेषामविशेषेण श्रूयते
25.2.m: "A brāhmaṇa should establish the fire at eight steps; a rājanya at eleven; a vaiśya at twelve; at twenty-four, [or] at an unlimited [distance], or as far as he may judge by eye, so that it is not established excessively far"—thus is it heard [in scripture] for all without distinction.
To the south, eastward, in the region beyond two thirds, closer to the Gārhapatya, it is known [from scripture] regarding the Dakṣiṇāgni.

25.2.s: gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantarālaṃ pañcadhā ṣaḍdhā vā saṃbhujya ṣaṣṭham̐ saptamaṃ vā bhāgamāgantumupasamasya samaṃ traidhaṃ vibhajya
25.2.d: गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरन्तरालं पञ्चधा षड्धा वा संभुज्य षष्ठँ सप्तमं वा भागमागन्तुमुपसमस्य समं त्रैधं विभज्य
25.2.m: Having folded the distance between the Gārhapatya and the Āhavanīya into five or into six, having added one-sixth or one-seventh part as an accession, having divided it equally into three,

25.2.s: aparasmidgastṛtīye lakṣaṇaṃ karoti gārhapatyāhavanīyayorantau niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya nimittaṃ karoti | dakṣiṇāgnerāyatanam̐ śrutisāmarthyāt
25.2.d: अपरस्मिद्गस्तृतीये लक्षणं करोति गार्हपत्याहवनीययोरन्तौ नियम्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य निमित्तं करोति । दक्षिणाग्नेरायतनँ श्रुतिसामर्थ्यात्
25.2.m: he makes a mark at the western third; having fixed the ends at the Gārhapatya and Āhavanīya, having stretched out southwards by the mark, he makes a sign. That is the site of the Dakṣiṇāgni, by virtue of scripture.

25.2.s: yajamānamātrī prācyaparimitā vā yathā'sannāni havīdgaṣi saṃbhavedevaṃ tiraścī prāñcau vedyadgasāvunnayatyabhita āhavanīyaṃ pratīcī śroṇī abhigārhapatyaṃ madhye saṃnatataraivamiva hi yoṣeti dārśikyā vedervijñāyate apareṇā havanīyaṃ yajamānamātraṃ dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya tāvatīṃ rajjumabhyasyobhayataḥ pāśau karoti | madhye lakṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇayoḥ śroṇyadgasayorantau niyamya lakṣaṇena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya nimittaṃ karoti | rajjuṃ niyamyāntau samasya dakṣiṇasyāḥ śroṇerdakṣiṇamadgasamālikhet | evamuttarataḥ | tiryaṅmānīṃ dviguṇāṃ tathā kṛtvā paścātpurastāccopalikhet vimitāyāṃ purastātpārśvamānyāvupasadgaharecchrutisāmarthyāt
25.2.d: यजमानमात्री प्राच्यपरिमिता वा यथाऽसन्नानि हवीद्गषि संभवेदेवं तिरश्ची प्राञ्चौ वेद्यद्गसावुन्नयत्यभित आहवनीयं प्रतीची श्रोणी अभिगार्हपत्यं मध्ये संनततरैवमिव हि योषेति दार्शिक्या वेदेर्विज्ञायते अपरेणा हवनीयं यजमानमात्रं दीर्घचतुरश्रं विहृत्य तावतीं रज्जुमभ्यस्योभयतः पाशौ करोति । मध्ये लक्षणं दक्षिणयोः श्रोण्यद्गसयोरन्तौ नियम्य लक्षणेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य निमित्तं करोति । रज्जुं नियम्यान्तौ समस्य दक्षिणस्याः श्रोणेर्दक्षिणमद्गसमालिखेत् । एवमुत्तरतः । तिर्यङ्मानीं द्विगुणां तथा कृत्वा पश्चात्पुरस्ताच्चोपलिखेत् विमितायां पुरस्तात्पार्श्वमान्यावुपसद्गहरेच्छ्रुतिसामर्थ्यात्
25.2.m: It is known [from scripture] regarding the New and Full Moon altar: "As long as the sacrificer's measure eastward or unlimited, so wide transversally that the oblations placed nearby can fit, he raises the two shoulders of the altar facing east around the Āhavanīya, the two buttocks facing west towards the Gārhapatya, contracted more in the middle, for indeed such is a woman." Having laid out a rectangle of the sacrificer's measure to the west of the Āhavanīya, having doubled that much cord, he makes loops at both ends. He makes a mark in the middle; having fixed the ends at the southern buttock and shoulder, having stretched out southwards by the mark, he makes a sign. Having fixed the cord, having brought the ends together, he should trace the southern shoulder from the southern buttock. Likewise on the north. Having made the transverse measure double in the same way, he should trace both on the west and on the east; when it has been measured out, he should bring the two lateral measures together in front, by virtue of scripture.

25.2.s: tridgaśatpadāni prakramā vā | paścāttiraścī bhavati ṣaṭtridgaśatprācī caturviṃdgaśatiḥ purastāttiraścīti saumikyā vedervijñāyate ṣaṭtriṃdgaśikāyāmaṣṭādaśopasamasyāparasmādantāddvādaśasu lakṣaṇaṃ pañcadaśasu lakṣaṇam | pṛṣṭhyāntayorantau niyamya pāñcadaśikena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya śaṅkue nihantyevamuttarataste śroṇī
25.2.d: त्रिद्गशत्पदानि प्रक्रमा वा । पश्चात्तिरश्ची भवति षट्त्रिद्गशत्प्राची चतुर्विंद्गशतिः पुरस्तात्तिरश्चीति सौमिक्या वेदेर्विज्ञायते षट्त्रिंद्गशिकायामष्टादशोपसमस्यापरस्मादन्ताद्द्वादशसु लक्षणं पञ्चदशसु लक्षणम् । पृष्ठ्यान्तयोरन्तौ नियम्य पाञ्चदशिकेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य शङ्कुए निहन्त्येवमुत्तरतस्ते श्रोणी

25.2.m: That is the laying out with a single cord. For [sides of] three and four, five is the diagonal cord.
By these multiplied by three, the two shoulders [are formed].
By these multiplied by four, the two buttocks [are formed].
For [sides of] twelve and five, thirteen is the diagonal cord; by these, the two shoulders [are formed].
By these multiplied by two, the two buttocks [are formed].
For [sides of] fifteen and eight, seventeen is the diagonal cord; by these, the two buttocks [are formed].
For [sides of] twelve and thirty-five, thirty-seven is the diagonal cord; by these, the two shoulders [are formed].
So many layings out of the altar are to be known.
The great altar is one thousand feet less twenty-eight.

25.2.s: dakṣiṇādadgasāddvādaśasu dakṣiṇasyādgaśroṇyāṃ nipātayecchedaṃ viparyasyetarata upadadhyāt | sā dīrghacaturaśrā mahāvedistathāyuktām̐ saṃcakṣīta
25.2.d: दक्षिणादद्गसाद्द्वादशसु दक्षिणस्याद्गश्रोण्यां निपातयेच्छेदं विपर्यस्येतरत उपदध्यात् । सा दीर्घचतुरश्रा महावेदिस्तथायुक्ताँ संचक्षीत
25.2.m: From the southern shoulder, he should drop [a perpendicular] at twelve on the southern buttock; having turned over the cut-off piece, he should place it on the other side. That great altar is a rectangle; he should consider it as arranged in that way.

25.2.s: saumikyā veditṛtīye yajata iti sautrāmaṇyā vijñāyate
25.2.d: सौमिक्या वेदितृतीये यजत इति सौत्रामण्या विज्ञायते
25.2.m: It is known [from scripture] regarding the Sautrāmaṇī: "He sacrifices on the third of the Soma altar."
The producing one-third of the step takes the place of the step.
Eight and ten are the two transverse measures.
The Sautrāmaṇī altar is three hundred and twenty-four feet.
And in the Aśvamedha it is known [from scripture]: "The altar is twice as large."
The producing double of the step takes the place of the step.
A step is two feet or three feet.
In the case of the step, there is optionality, because the meaning of the word is dubious.
for he is the performer of the actions.
It is known [from scripture]: "The altar of the independent animal sacrifice is chariot-sized."

25.2.s: ratheṣāmātrī prācī rathākṣamātrī paścāttiraścī vipathayugamātrī purastāttiraścī
25.2.d: रथेषामात्री प्राची रथाक्षमात्री पश्चात्तिरश्ची विपथयुगमात्री पुरस्तात्तिरश्ची
25.2.m: Eastward it is the size of the chariot pole; westward it is transversally the size of the chariot axle; eastward it is transversally the size of the yoke of a cart.

25.2.s: yāvatā vā bāhye chidre | tadekarajjvoktaṃ pañcadaśikenaivāpāyamya
25.2.d: यावता वा बाह्ये छिद्रे । तदेकरज्ज्वोक्तं पञ्चदशिकेनैवापायम्य
25.2.m: Or as much as [the distance between] the outer holes. That is explained with a single cord, having stretched out by the fifteen-[part mark] alone.
He should extend the buttocks and shoulders by half an axle and half a yoke.

25.2.s: aṣṭāśītiśatamīṣā tiryagakṣaścatuḥśatam̐ ṣaḍaśītiryugamāhuḥ | sa rathaścāraṇa ucyata iti rathaparimāṇam
25.2.d: अष्टाशीतिशतमीषा तिर्यगक्षश्चतुःशतँ षडशीतिर्युगमाहुः । स रथश्चारण उच्यत इति रथपरिमाणम्
25.2.m: "A pole is one hundred and eighty-eight; an axle across is one hundred and four; eighty-six, they say, is the yoke; that chariot is called moving"—this is the chariot measurement.

25.2.s: aratnibhirvā ṣaḍbhiḥprācī | caturbhiḥ paścāttiraścī tribhiḥ purastāttiraścī tadekarajjvoktamadhyardhe rajjau dvayorardhatṛtīyayoḥ ṣaṭsviti lakṣaṇāni karoti navasu pāśaṃ pṛṣṭhyāntayorantau niyamyārdhatṛtīyakena dakṣiṇā'pāyamya dvayoḥ śaṅkue nihantyevamuttarataste śroṇī viparyastayā'dgasau tenaivāpāyamyādhyardhe śaṅkue nihanti | evamuttaratastāvadgasau | daśapadottaravedirbhavediti some vijñāyate
25.2.d: अरत्निभिर्वा षड्भिःप्राची । चतुर्भिः पश्चात्तिरश्ची त्रिभिः पुरस्तात्तिरश्ची तदेकरज्ज्वोक्तमध्यर्धे रज्जौ द्वयोरर्धतृतीययोः षट्स्विति लक्षणानि करोति नवसु पाशं पृष्ठ्यान्तयोरन्तौ नियम्यार्धतृतीयकेन दक्षिणाऽपायम्य द्वयोः शङ्कुए निहन्त्येवमुत्तरतस्ते श्रोणी विपर्यस्तयाऽद्गसौ तेनैवापायम्याध्यर्धे शङ्कुए निहन्ति । एवमुत्तरतस्तावद्गसौ । दशपदोत्तरवेदिर्भवेदिति सोमे विज्ञायते

25.2.m: That is explained with a single cord: having stretched out by the fifteen-[part mark] alone, he should then extend the buttocks and shoulders by half.
When it has been measured out, he should bring the two lateral measures together in front,

25.2.s: pade yuge'ratnāviyati prādeśe prakrame śamyāyāṃ ca mānārtheṣu yāthākāmī śabdārthasya viśayitvāt
25.2.d: पदे युगेऽरत्नावियति प्रादेशे प्रक्रमे शम्यायां च मानार्थेषु याथाकामी शब्दार्थस्य विशयित्वात्
25.2.m: With regard to the foot, the yoke, the cubit, the span, the step, and the yoke-pin as measures, there is optionality, because the meaning of the word is dubious.
It is known [from scripture] regarding the ancestral altar: "It is of the sacrificer's measure and four-cornered."
That is explained with a single cord: having stretched out by the fifteen-[part mark] alone, he should then extend the buttocks and shoulders by half.
It is known [from scripture] regarding the sadas hall: "It is nine cubits across and twenty-seven long northward."
"Eighteen," according to some. That is explained with a single cord: having stretched out by the fifteen-[part mark] alone, he should extend the buttocks and shoulders by four and a half.
It is known [from scripture] regarding the resonance holes: "They have spans as their mouths and are spaced a span apart."

25.2.s: aratnimātraṃ caturaśraṃ vihṛtya sraktiṣu śaṅkue nihatyārdhaprādeśena taṃ taṃ parilikhecchrutisāmarthyāt
25.2.d: अरत्निमात्रं चतुरश्रं विहृत्य स्रक्तिषु शङ्कुए निहत्यार्धप्रादेशेन तं तं परिलिखेच्छ्रुतिसामर्थ्यात्

25.2.m: It is known [from scripture] regarding the Gārhapatya layer: "It is of the reach of the outstretched arms and four-cornered."
"Square," according to some; "circular," according to others.

25.2.s: karaṇaṃ vyāyāmasya tṛtīyāyāmam̐ saptamaṃ vyāsaṃ kārayet
25.2.d: करणं व्यायामस्य तृतीयायामँ सप्तमं व्यासं कारयेत्
25.2.m: The preparation: he should cause [bricks] to be made of one-third the outstretched arms in length and one-seventh in width.
They are twenty-one.
In laying down, they are oriented eastward in the first layer; in the other [layer], they are oriented northward.

25.2.s: maṇḍalāyāṃ mṛdo dehaṃ kṛtvā madhye śaṅkue nihatyārdhavyāyāmena maṇḍalaṃ parilikhet
25.2.d: मण्डलायां मृदो देहं कृत्वा मध्ये शङ्कुए निहत्यार्धव्यायामेन मण्डलं परिलिखेत्

25.2.m: Having drawn lines dividing that into nine,
having divided each segment into three, that is laid down.
He should arrange the corners towards the intermediate directions of the square.
In the other layer, [they should face] the cardinal directions.

25.2.s: piśīlamātrā bhavantīti dhiṣṇiyānāṃ vijñāyate caturaśrā ityekeṣām - parimaṇḍalā ityekeṣām
25.2.d: पिशीलमात्रा भवन्तीति धिष्णियानां विज्ञायते चतुरश्रा इत्येकेषाम् - परिमण्डला इत्येकेषाम्
25.2.m: “They are of the size of a bowl,” it is known regarding the dhiṣṇyas; “square,” say some; “circular,” say some.

25.2.s: āgnīdhrīyaṃ navadhā vyavalikhyaikasyāḥ sthāne'śmānamavadhāya yathāsaṃkhyamitarānvyavalikhya yathāyogamupadadhyāt
25.2.d: आग्नीध्रीयं नवधा व्यवलिख्यैकस्याः स्थानेऽश्मानमवधाय यथासंख्यमितरान्व्यवलिख्य यथायोगमुपदध्यात्
25.2.m: having marked out the Āgnīdhrīya in nine parts, placing a stone in the place of one, and having marked out the others according to their number, he should lay [them] appropriately.

25.3.s: bhavatīva khalu vā eṣa yo'gniṃ cinuta iti vijñāyate
25.3.d: भवतीव खलु वा एष योऽग्निं चिनुत इति विज्ञायते
25.3.m: “He indeed, as it were, comes into being who piles the fire-altar,” so it is known [from scripture].

25.3.s: vayasāṃ yā eṣa pratimayā cīyata ityākṛticodanāt
25.3.d: वयसां या एष प्रतिमया चीयत इत्याकृतिचोदनात्
25.3.m: Because of the injunction of the form: “This [fire-altar] is piled in the likeness of a bird.”
Or by direct precept, [it is constructed] with as much as is handed down in the sacred texts.

25.3.s: veṇunā sapta puruṣānvimimīte trīnprācaḥ puruṣādgaścaturudīcastiryañcaṃ puruṣamātrāṇi pakṣapucchāni bhavanti | ātmā catuṣpuruṣaḥ
25.3.d: वेणुना सप्त पुरुषान्विमिमीते त्रीन्प्राचः पुरुषाद्गश्चतुरुदीचस्तिर्यञ्चं पुरुषमात्राणि पक्षपुच्छानि भवन्ति । आत्मा चतुष्पुरुषः
25.3.m: With a bamboo cane he measures out seven puruṣas: three puruṣas eastwards, four puruṣas transversely northwards; the wings and the tail are one puruṣa [square] each; the body is four puruṣas [in area].
By a cubit he lengthens the southern wing to the south.
By a span or a short span, [he lengthens] the tail to the west.
By a cubit, the northern wing [to the north].

25.3.s: ekavidhaḥ prathamo'gniḥ dvividho dvitīyaḥ | trividhastṛtīyaḥ | ta evamevodyantyaikaśatavidhāt
25.3.d: एकविधः प्रथमोऽग्निः द्विविधो द्वितीयः । त्रिविधस्तृतीयः । त एवमेवोद्यन्त्यैकशतविधात्
25.3.m: The first fire-altar is single-fold; the second is twofold; the third is threefold; thus they increase up to a hundredfold.
Indeed, he should pile it only as sevenfold.
“The archetype fire-altar is sevenfold, thereafter [are] those increased by one each,” it is known.
Those beginning with the single-fold do not have wings and tails,
because [the description of wings and tails] is supplementary to the statement of the sevenfold [fire-altar],
and because of contradiction with the revealed text.
For those beginning with the eightfold, dividing whatever is other than the seven [puruṣas] into seven parts, he should distribute [one share] to each puruṣa,
because no modification of the form is revealed in scripture.

25.3.s: puruṣamātreṇa vimimīte veṇunā vimimīta iti vijñāyate
25.3.d: पुरुषमात्रेण विमिमीते वेणुना विमिमीत इति विज्ञायते
25.3.m: “He measures by a puruṣa; he measures with a bamboo cane,” so it is known.
As tall as the sacrificer is with his arms raised, at that distance he makes two holes in the bamboo cane.
Having placed the bamboo cane pointing east along the east-west axis to the west of the place of the sacrificial post's pit,

25.3.s: chidreṣu śaṅkūnnihatyonmucyāparābhyāṃ dakṣiṇā prāk parilikhet | ā'ntādunmucya pūrvasmādaparasminpratimucya dakṣiṇā pratyakparilikhedā'ntāt
25.3.d: छिद्रेषु शङ्कून्निहत्योन्मुच्यापराभ्यां दक्षिणा प्राक् परिलिखेत् । आऽन्तादुन्मुच्य पूर्वस्मादपरस्मिन्प्रतिमुच्य दक्षिणा प्रत्यक्परिलिखेदाऽन्तात्
25.3.m: having driven pegs into the holes, freeing [the bamboo] from the western two [pegs], he traces [a line] south-eastwards to the end; freeing [it] from the eastern [peg] and fastening [it] to the western one, he traces [a line] south-westwards to the end.

25.3.s: unmucya veṇuṃ madhyame śaṅkāvantyacchidraṃ pratimucyoparyupari lekhāsamaraṃ dakṣiṇāṃ veṇuṃ nidhāyāntye chidre śaṅkue nihatya tasminmadhyamacchidraṃ pratimucya lekhāntayoritare pratiṣṭhāpya cchidrayoḥ śaṅkū nihanti | sa puruṣaścaturaśraḥ
25.3.d: उन्मुच्य वेणुं मध्यमे शङ्कावन्त्यच्छिद्रं प्रतिमुच्योपर्युपरि लेखासमरं दक्षिणां वेणुं निधायान्त्ये छिद्रे शङ्कुए निहत्य तस्मिन्मध्यमच्छिद्रं प्रतिमुच्य लेखान्तयोरितरे प्रतिष्ठाप्य च्छिद्रयोः शङ्कू निहन्ति । स पुरुषश्चतुरश्रः

25.3.m: In this manner, turning clockwise, he measures out four puruṣas in the body;

25.3.s: puruṣaṃ dakṣiṇe pakṣe puruṣaṃ pucche puruṣamuttare
25.3.d: पुरुषं दक्षिणे पक्षे पुरुषं पुच्छे पुरुषमुत्तरे
25.3.m: a puruṣa for the southern wing, a puruṣa for the tail, and a puruṣa for the northern [wing].
It has been stated: “by a cubit [he lengthens] the southern [wing] to the south.”

25.3.s: pṛṣṭhyāto vā puruṣamātrasyākṣṇayā veṇuṃ nidhāya pūrvasminnitaraṃ tābhyāṃ dakṣiṇamadgasaṃ nirharet
25.3.d: पृष्ठ्यातो वा पुरुषमात्रस्याक्ष्णया वेणुं निधाय पूर्वस्मिन्नितरं ताभ्यां दक्षिणमद्गसं निर्हरेत्
25.3.m: Or, having placed the bamboo cane diagonally from the east-west axis for the length of a puruṣa, and the other to the east, with these two he should determine the southern shoulder;
as before, the northern shoulder.
Or, having measured with a cord according to the rule of the high altar, he measures out with a bamboo cane.

25.3.s: sapakṣapuccheṣu vidhābhyāse'pacaye ca vidhāsaptamakaraṇīṃ puruṣasthānīyāṃ kṛtvā tayā viharet
25.3.d: सपक्षपुच्छेषु विधाभ्यासेऽपचये च विधासप्तमकरणीं पुरुषस्थानीयां कृत्वा तया विहरेत्
25.3.m: In the repetition and reduction of the forms with wings and tail, having made the side producing one-seventh of the form take the place of a puruṣa, he should lay out [the altar] with it.
He should have the molds of the bricks made with the fifth of a puruṣa.
Those that are one and a half [times this] on one side are the second [kind].

25.3.s: purusya pañcamo bhāga ekataḥ prādeśa ekatastattṛtīyam
25.3.d: पुरुस्य पञ्चमो भाग एकतः प्रादेश एकतस्तत्तृतीयम्
25.3.m: One-fifth part of a puruṣa on one side and a span on the other side is the third [kind].
A span on all sides is the fourth [kind]; squares of one-fifteenth part [of a puruṣa] are the fifth [kind].
The height measure of the bricks: he should have [them] made with a fifth of a knee-height.
With half [that height] for the nākasad and the pañcacoḍā bricks.
Whatever shrinks when being baked, he should fill that up with loose earth,
because the loose earth has no fixed measure.
In laying down [the bricks], he should lay ten one-and-a-half bricks in the east of the body, facing west,

25.3.s: pañca pañca pakṣāgrayoḥ pakṣāpyayayośca viśayāstāsāmardheṣṭakāmātrāṇi pakṣayorbhavanti
25.3.d: पञ्च पञ्च पक्षाग्रयोः पक्षाप्यययोश्च विशयास्तासामर्धेष्टकामात्राणि पक्षयोर्भवन्ति
25.3.m: Five [are laid] each at the tips of the wings and at the joints of the wings across [the line of junction]; halves of those bricks are in the two wings.

25.3.s: pañca pañca pucchapārśvayordakṣiṇāḥ udīcīśca pucche prādeśamupadhāya
25.3.d: पञ्च पञ्च पुच्छपार्श्वयोर्दक्षिणाः उदीचीश्च पुच्छे प्रादेशमुपधाय
25.3.m: Five each on both sides of the tail, facing south and north, having laid span-[bricks] in the tail.
He should cover the entire fire-altar with fifth-part bricks.
He should complete the number with fifteenth-part bricks.
In the other layer, he should lay ten one-and-a-half bricks in the body on the south facing north, and ten on the north facing south.

25.3.s: yathā prathame prastāre pakṣau tathā puccham | yathā pucche tathā pakṣau | viparītā'pyaye
25.3.d: यथा प्रथमे प्रस्तारे पक्षौ तथा पुच्छम् । यथा पुच्छे तथा पक्षौ । विपरीताऽप्यये

25.3.s: sarvamagniṃ pañcamabhāgīyābhiḥ pracchādayet | pañcadaśabhāgīyābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet
25.3.d: सर्वमग्निं पञ्चमभागीयाभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । पञ्चदशभागीयाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत्
25.3.m: He should cover the entire fire-altar with fifth-part bricks; he should complete the number with fifteenth-part bricks.

25.3.s: pañca citayo bhavanti pañcabhiḥ purīṣairabhyūhatīti vijñāyate | purīṣāntā citirarthāntaratvātpurīṣasya
25.3.d: पञ्च चितयो भवन्ति पञ्चभिः पुरीषैरभ्यूहतीति विज्ञायते । पुरीषान्ता चितिरर्थान्तरत्वात्पुरीषस्य
25.3.m: “There are five layers; he covers them with five [layers of] loose earth,” so it is known; a layer ends with loose earth, because loose earth is a distinct entity.
Piling for the first time, he should pile a thousand [bricks] knee-deep;
the second time, two thousand [bricks] navel-deep;
the third time, three thousand [bricks] mouth-deep.

25.3.s: uttaramuttaraṃ jyāyādgasaṃ mahāntaṃ bṛhantamaparimitaṃ svargakāmaścinvīteti vijñāyate
25.3.d: उत्तरमुत्तरं ज्यायाद्गसं महान्तं बृहन्तमपरिमितं स्वर्गकामश्चिन्वीतेति विज्ञायते
25.3.m: “Each subsequent one larger, great, vast, immeasurable, one who desires heaven should pile,” so it is known.

25.3.s: dviṣāhasre dviprastārāścitayo bhavanti | triṣāhasre triprastārāḥ | caturthaprabhṛtyāhāreṣu nityamiṣṭakāparimāṇam
25.3.d: द्विषाहस्रे द्विप्रस्ताराश्चितयो भवन्ति । त्रिषाहस्रे त्रिप्रस्ताराः । चतुर्थप्रभृत्याहारेषु नित्यमिष्टकापरिमाणम्
25.3.m: In the two-thousand [fire-altar] the layers consist of two layer-arrangements; in the three-thousand [fire-altar] they consist of three layer-arrangements; in additions from the fourth onward, the measure of the bricks is constant.

25.3.s: vijñāyate ca na jyāyādgasaṃ citvā kanīyādgasaṃ cinvīteti
25.3.d: विज्ञायते च न ज्यायाद्गसं चित्वा कनीयाद्गसं चिन्वीतेति
25.3.m: And it is taught [in the Veda]: "Having piled a larger [altar], one must not pile a smaller one."

25.4.m: It is taught [in the Veda]: "He piles the fire with quadrilaterals."
[They are] squares, because the word is without an additional qualification.

25.4.s: pādamātryo bhavanti | aṇūkamātryo bhavanti ūrvasthimātryo bhavanti | aratnimātryo bhavanti | prādeśamātryo bhavantīti vijñāyate
25.4.d: पादमात्र्यो भवन्ति । अणूकमात्र्यो भवन्ति ऊर्वस्थिमात्र्यो भवन्ति । अरत्निमात्र्यो भवन्ति । प्रादेशमात्र्यो भवन्तीति विज्ञायते
25.4.m: It is taught [in the Veda]: "They are foot-sized; they are spine-sized; they are thigh-bone-sized; they are cubit-sized; they are span-sized."
A fourth-part [brick] is the spine; a fifth-part [brick] is the cubit, and likewise the thigh-bone.

25.4.s: pādeṣṭakā pādamātrī | tatra yāthākāmī śabdārthasya viśayitvāt
25.4.d: पादेष्टका पादमात्री । तत्र याथाकामी शब्दार्थस्य विशयित्वात्
25.4.m: The quarter-brick is foot-sized. In that matter, there is free choice, because the meaning of the word is uncertain.
In the laying down, one should place eight quarter-bricks of the fourth-part [bricks] at each of the two wing-tips;
and similarly at the two joints [connecting the wings] to the body, combined with six finger-breadths;
at the buttock [corners] and shoulder [corners], eight pointing east and [eight] pointing west;
in the space between the joints, fifth-part [bricks] with a quarter.
Having laid down span-sized [bricks] on the tail,
he should cover the entire fire with fourth-part [bricks].
In the other layer arrangement, at the junction of the tail, fifth-part [bricks] are placed crosswise;
these he should lay down all around on the body as appropriate with fourteen quarter-[bricks].
He should cover the entire fire with fifth-part [bricks]; he should complete the number with quarter-bricks.

25.4.s: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ karaṇīṃ dvādaśena trayodaśena veṣṭakāḥ kārayet
25.4.d: एकविधप्रभृतीनां करणीं द्वादशेन त्रयोदशेन वेष्टकाः कारयेत्
25.4.m: For [altars] beginning with the one-fold, he should make bricks with a twelfth or a thirteenth [part] of the producing side,

25.4.s: ekavidhaprabhṛtīnāṃ prathamāhāreṇa dvitīyena tṛtīyena yo yujyeta sarveṣāṃ yathāśruti saṃkhyā tathordhvapramāṇam
25.4.d: एकविधप्रभृतीनां प्रथमाहारेण द्वितीयेन तृतीयेन यो युज्येत सर्वेषां यथाश्रुति संख्या तथोर्ध्वप्रमाणम्
25.4.m: For [altars] beginning with the one-fold, whichever is combined with the first, the second, or the third intake, the number of all [bricks] is according to the Vedic text, and likewise the vertical measure.
The optional [altars] are modifications of attributes, because the rules are for attributes.
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who has a rival should pile the triangle-shaped altar."

25.4.s: yāvānagniḥ sāratniprādeśo dvistāvatīṃ bhūmiṃ caturaśrāṃ kṛtvā
25.4.d: यावानग्निः सारत्निप्रादेशो द्विस्तावतीं भूमिं चतुरश्रां कृत्वा
25.4.m: Having made a square ground twice as large as the fire with the cubit and span,

25.4.s: pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhācchroṇī pratyālikhetsā nityā praugam
25.4.d: पूर्वस्याः करण्या अर्धाच्छ्रोणी प्रत्यालिखेत्सा नित्या प्रौगम्
25.4.m: from the middle of the eastern producing side, one should draw lines toward the two buttock [corners]; that is the constant triangle-shaped altar.
The rules for construction and piling are as stated for the one-fold [altar].
He should make triangular bricks.

25.4.s: ubhayataḥpraugaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta sajātān bhrātṛvyānnudeya pratijaniṣyamāṇāniti vijñāyate | ubhayataḥ śakaṭākṛtirbhavati
25.4.d: उभयतःप्रौगं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत सजातान् भ्रातृव्यान्नुदेय प्रतिजनिष्यमाणानिति विज्ञायते । उभयतः शकटाकृतिर्भवति
25.4.m: It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who wishes 'May I drive away the born and the yet-to-be-born rivals of my own kin' should pile the double-triangle-shaped altar." It has the form of a double cart-chassis.

25.4.s: yathā vimukhe śakaṭe tadetadeva dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya pūrvāparayoḥ karaṇyorarthāttāvati dakṣiṇottarayoniṃpātayetsā nityobhayataḥpraugaḥ
25.4.d: यथा विमुखे शकटे तदेतदेव दीर्घचतुरश्रं विहृत्य पूर्वापरयोः करण्योरर्थात्तावति दक्षिणोत्तरयोनिंपातयेत्सा नित्योभयतःप्रौगः
25.4.m: Like two carts with unyoked oxen face to face; having laid out that very same rectangle, from the middle of the eastern and western producing sides, he should cause [lines] to fall at that distance to the southern and northern points; that is the constant double-triangle-shaped altar.
As stated for the triangle-shaped altar, he should make double-triangle bricks.

25.4.s: rathacakracitaṃ cinvīta bhrātṛvyavāniti vijñāyate | parimaṇḍalo bhavati
25.4.d: रथचक्रचितं चिन्वीत भ्रातृव्यवानिति विज्ञायते । परिमण्डलो भवति
25.4.m: It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who has a rival should pile the chariot-wheel-shaped altar." It is circular.
Having made the ground circular, as large as the fire with the cubit and span,

25.4.s: tasya karaṇyā dvādaśeneṣṭakāḥ kārayettāsām̐ ṣaṭpradhāvupadhāya śeṣamaṣṭadhā vibhajet
25.4.d: तस्य करण्या द्वादशेनेष्टकाः कारयेत्तासाँ षट्प्रधावुपधाय शेषमष्टधा विभजेत्
25.4.m: With a twelfth [part] of its producing side he should make bricks; having placed six of them in the segment [of the circle], he should divide the remainder into eight parts.

25.4.s: upadhāne caturaśrasyāvāntaradeśānprati sraktīḥ saṃpādayet | madhyānītarasminprastāre vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādyāvataḥ prastārādgaścikīrṣet
25.4.d: उपधाने चतुरश्रस्यावान्तरदेशान्प्रति स्रक्तीः संपादयेत् । मध्यानीतरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे व्यत्यासं चिनुयाद्यावतः प्रस्ताराद्गश्चिकीर्षेत्
25.4.m: In the laying down, he should make the corners face the intermediate regions of the square; in the other layer arrangement, the middles. He should pile alternating [layers], for as many layer arrangements as he wishes to make.
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who desires food should pile the trough-shaped altar."
The handle is one-tenth of the entire ground.
Its reduction has been explained by [that of] the tail.
With a twelfth [part] of its producing side he should make bricks,
and one-and-a-half-sized [bricks] and quarter-bricks.

25.4.s: upadhāne'dhyardhāḥpurastāt pratīcīrātmanyupadadhyāt | tsarvagre śroṇyośca prācīḥ sarvamagniṃ caturaśrābhiḥ pracchādayet | pādeṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet aparasminprastāre'dhyardhā daśa dakṣiṇata udīcīrātmanyupadadhāti uttarataśca dakṣiṇā tsarupārśvayordakṣiṇā udīcīśca sarvamagniṃ caturaśrābhiḥ pracchādayet | pādeṣṭakābhiḥ saṃkhyāṃ pūrayet | vyatyāsaṃ cinuyādyāvataḥ prastārādgaścikīrṣet
25.4.d: उपधानेऽध्यर्धाःपुरस्तात् प्रतीचीरात्मन्युपदध्यात् । त्सर्वग्रे श्रोण्योश्च प्राचीः सर्वमग्निं चतुरश्राभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । पादेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारेऽध्यर्धा दश दक्षिणत उदीचीरात्मन्युपदधाति उत्तरतश्च दक्षिणा त्सरुपार्श्वयोर्दक्षिणा उदीचीश्च सर्वमग्निं चतुरश्राभिः प्रच्छादयेत् । पादेष्टकाभिः संख्यां पूरयेत् । व्यत्यासं चिनुयाद्यावतः प्रस्ताराद्गश्चिकीर्षेत्
25.4.m: In the laying down, he should lay down one-and-a-half-sized [bricks] in front, facing west, on the body; at the tip of the handle and at the two buttock [corners], [bricks] facing east. He should cover the entire fire with quadrilaterals; he should complete the number with quarter-bricks. In the other layer arrangement, he lays down ten one-and-a-half-sized [bricks] in the south, facing north, on the body, and in the north, facing south; and on the two sides of the handle, [bricks] facing south and north. He should cover the entire fire with quadrilaterals; he should complete the number with quarter-bricks. He should pile alternating [layers], for as many layer arrangements as he wishes to make.
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who desires cattle should pile the gathered-heap altar."
He lays down bricks as if gathering them together into a heap.
"Having dug rubbish-pit holes in the cardinal directions, he heaps up soil from them"—according to some [teachers].
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who desires a village community should pile the circularly piled altar."

25.4.s: madhyamām̐ svayamātṛṇṇāṃ pradakṣiṇamiṣṭakāgaṇaiḥ paricinoti sa paricāyyaḥ
25.4.d: मध्यमाँ स्वयमातृण्णां प्रदक्षिणमिष्टकागणैः परिचिनोति स परिचाय्यः
25.4.m: He piles [bricks] all around the middle naturally perforated brick in a clockwise direction with groups of bricks: that is the circularly piled altar.
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who desires cattle should pile the sequentially piled altar."

25.4.s: paricāyyenoktaḥ śmaśānacitaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta pitṛloka ṛdhnuyāmiti vijñāyate
25.4.d: परिचाय्येनोक्तः श्मशानचितं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत पितृलोक ऋध्नुयामिति विज्ञायते
25.4.m: It is explained by the circularly piled altar. It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who wishes 'May I prosper in the world of the ancestors' should pile the cemetery-shaped altar."

25.4.s: dvayāni khalu śmaśānacitāni caturaśrāṇi parimaṇḍalāni ca tatra yāthākāmī śabdārthasya ca viśayitvāt
25.4.d: द्वयानि खलु श्मशानचितानि चतुरश्राणि परिमण्डलानि च तत्र याथाकामी शब्दार्थस्य च विशयित्वात्
25.4.m: Indeed, the cemetery-shaped altars are of two kinds: quadrilaterals and circles; in that matter, there is free choice, because the meaning of the word is uncertain.

25.4.s: caturaśraṃ vā yasya guṇaśāstraṃ ca caturaśraḥ
25.4.d: चतुरश्रं वा यस्य गुणशास्त्रं च चतुरश्रः
25.4.m: Or [it is] a quadrilateral, for whom the rule of attributes is a quadrilateral.
It is explained by the trough-shaped altar, excluding the handle.
It is taught [in the Veda]: "He who desires cattle should pile the meter-shaped altar."
"He should pile with all the meters," says one [view]; "with the primary [meters]," says another.

25.5.s: evamiva hi vayasāṃ madhye pakṣinirṇāmo bhavatīti vijñāyate
25.5.d: एवमिव हि वयसां मध्ये पक्षिनिर्णामो भवतीति विज्ञायते
25.5.m: "For thus indeed the bending of the wings occurs in the middle in birds," so it is known.
As large as the fire [altar] is, with the cubit and span, it amounts to sevenfold.
A span, a fourth [of a puruṣa] of the body, and eight quarter-sized [bricks];
one should divide the remainder between the two wings.
A vyāyāma is four cubits; a cubit is twenty-four finger-breadths.
Half of that is a span: such is the determination.
Nine and a half cubits, less one quarter-part of a finger-breadth, is the length of a wing.
He makes a cord of two puruṣas with loops at both ends;

25.5.s: pakṣasyāparayoḥ koṭyoranto niyamya lakṣaṇena prācīnamāyacchedevaṃ purastātsanirṇāma etenottaraḥ pakṣo vyākhyātaḥ
25.5.d: पक्षस्यापरयोः कोट्योरन्तो नियम्य लक्षणेन प्राचीनमायच्छेदेवं पुरस्तात्सनिर्णाम एतेनोत्तरः पक्षो व्याख्यातः
25.5.m: Fixing the [two] ends at the two western corners of the wing, he should stretch [it] eastward by the mark; in the same way at the front, with the bending. By this the northern wing is explained.
The body is two puruṣas in length and one and a half puruṣas in breadth.
At the tail, he should stretch [a rectangle] of a puruṣa westward with a breadth of half a puruṣa.
To the south of it another, and to the north [another].
One should draw the two diagonally, so that half a puruṣa is at the junction.

25.5.s: śirasyardhapuruṣeṇa caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhāttāviti dakṣiṇottarayornipātayet
25.5.d: शिरस्यर्धपुरुषेण चतुरश्रं कृत्वा पूर्वस्याः करण्या अर्धात्ताविति दक्षिणोत्तरयोर्निपातयेत्
25.5.m: Having made a square of half a puruṣa at the head, he should drop [cords] from the middle of the eastern producing side to that extent on the south and the north.
Towards the junctions, he should cut off the buttocks and shoulders.

25.5.s: karaṇaṃ puruṣasya pañcamāyāmam̐ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vyāsaṃ kārayedyathāyoganataṃ tatprathamam
25.5.d: करणं पुरुषस्य पञ्चमायामँ षष्ठं व्यासं कारयेद्यथायोगनतं तत्प्रथमम्
25.5.m: He should have made the brick with a fifth [of a puruṣa] as length and a sixth as breadth, bent as required: that is the first [brick].
Two of them joined eastward: that is the second.
One should increase one-sixth of the first by an eighth, bent as required: that is the third.
One and a half of the quarter-part [brick]; one should divide diagonally an amount equal to a quarter-part of it: that is the fourth.
Half of the quarter-part [brick] is the fifth.
Its diagonal division is the sixth.

25.5.s: puruṣasya pañcamabhāgaṃ daśabhāgaṃ vyāsaṃ pratīcīnamāyacchet | tasya dakṣiṇato'nyamuttarataśca tāvakṣṇayā dakṣiṇāparayoḥ koṭyorālikhettatsaptamam
25.5.d: पुरुषस्य पञ्चमभागं दशभागं व्यासं प्रतीचीनमायच्छेत् । तस्य दक्षिणतोऽन्यमुत्तरतश्च तावक्ष्णया दक्षिणापरयोः कोट्योरालिखेत्तत्सप्तमम्
25.5.m: He should stretch westward a fifth part of a puruṣa [in length] with a tenth part as breadth; another to the south of it and to the north; he should draw them diagonally to the south-western corners: that is the seventh.
Thus the other northern one is to be known: one should draw it from the northern corner: that is the eighth.
The division on both sides diagonally of the quarter-part [brick] is the ninth.

25.5.s: upadhāne ṣaṣṭiḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ pakṣayoḥ prathamā udīcīrnidadhyāt
25.5.d: उपधाने षष्टिः षष्टिः पक्षयोः प्रथमा उदीचीर्निदध्यात्
25.5.m: In laying down, he should place sixty, sixty of the first [bricks] facing north on the two wings.
On the two sides of the tail, eight, eight of the sixth [bricks];
—three at the tip, then one, then three, then one.
At the tail junction, two fourth [bricks] lying across;
and behind them, two fifth [bricks] joined at their edges.
At the buttocks and shoulders, eight [bricks] facing east and facing west.
And in the remainder, twenty-six [first bricks], eight sixth [bricks], four fifth [bricks].
At the head, two fourth [bricks] lying across, and in front of them two facing east.
In the other layer, five, five of the second [bricks] at the bends of the wings;
and at the two junctions, two third [bricks]; these are eighth-parts of the body.
In the remainder, he should place forty-five, forty-five of the first [bricks] facing east.
On the two sides of the tail, five, five of the seventh [bricks];
and on either side of the second and fourth [rows], one each joined together.
In the remainder, thirteen eighth [bricks].
At the buttocks and shoulders, eight fourth [bricks] facing south and north.
And in the remainder, twenty [first bricks], thirty sixth [bricks], one fifth [brick].
At the head, two fourth [bricks], and in front of them four ninth [bricks].

25.6.s: evamiva hi vayasāṃ madhye pakṣanirṇāmo bhavatīti vijñāyate
25.6.d: एवमिव हि वयसां मध्ये पक्षनिर्णामो भवतीति विज्ञायते
25.6.m: "For thus indeed the bending of the wings occurs in the middle in birds," so it is known.

25.6.s: puruṣasya ṣoḍaśībhirvidgaśam̐ śatam̐ sāratniprādeśaḥ saptavidhaḥ saṃpadyate | tāsāṃ catvāridgaśadātmani tisraḥ śirasi pañcadaśa puccha ekatridgaśaddakṣiṇe pakṣe | tathottare
25.6.d: पुरुषस्य षोडशीभिर्विद्गशँ शतँ सारत्निप्रादेशः सप्तविधः संपद्यते । तासां चत्वारिद्गशदात्मनि तिस्रः शिरसि पञ्चदश पुच्छ एकत्रिद्गशद्दक्षिणे पक्षे । तथोत्तरे
25.6.m: By sixteenths of a puruṣa, one hundred and twenty amounts to sevenfold with the cubit and span. Of them, forty are in the body, three in the head, fifteen in the tail, thirty-one in the southern wing; likewise in the northern.

25.6.s: adhyardhapuruṣāstiryagdvāvāyāmata iti dīrghacaturaśraṃ vihṛtya śroṇyadgasebhyo dve dve ṣoḍaśyau nirasyet
25.6.d: अध्यर्धपुरुषास्तिर्यग्द्वावायामत इति दीर्घचतुरश्रं विहृत्य श्रोण्यद्गसेभ्यो द्वे द्वे षोडश्यौ निरस्येत्
25.6.m: Having laid out a rectangle of one and a half puruṣas transversely and two in length, he should remove two sixteenths each from the buttocks and shoulders.

25.6.s: catvāridgaśatpariśiṣyante | sa ātmā śirasyardhapuruṣeṇa caturaśraṃ kṛtvā pūrvasyāḥ karaṇyā ardhāttāvati dakṣiṇottarayornipātayet
25.6.d: चत्वारिद्गशत्परिशिष्यन्ते । स आत्मा शिरस्यर्धपुरुषेण चतुरश्रं कृत्वा पूर्वस्याः करण्या अर्धात्तावति दक्षिणोत्तरयोर्निपातयेत्
25.6.m: Forty remain. That is the body. Having made a square of half a puruṣa at the head, he should drop [cords] from the middle of the eastern producing side to that extent on the south and the north.
Three remain: that is the head.
A puruṣa transversely, two in length, and one-sixteenth: that is the right wing.

25.6.s: tathottaraḥ pakṣāgre puruṣacaturthena catvāri caturaśrāṇi kṛtvā tānyakṣṇayā vyavalikhyārdhāni nirasyet
25.6.d: तथोत्तरः पक्षाग्रे पुरुषचतुर्थेन चत्वारि चतुरश्राणि कृत्वा तान्यक्ष्णया व्यवलिख्यार्धानि निरस्येत्
25.6.m: Likewise the left. Having made four squares at the tip of the wing with one-fourth of a puruṣa, having drawn their diagonals, one should cast off half of each.
Thirty-one remain.
Leaving aside the wing tip, one should draw an eastward line in the middle of the wing.

25.6.s: pakṣāpyaye puruṣaṃ niyamya lekhāyāṃ puruṣānte nitodaṃ kuryānnitodāt prācīnaṃ puruṣānte nitodayornānāntāvālikhettatsaṃnamanam
25.6.d: पक्षाप्यये पुरुषं नियम्य लेखायां पुरुषान्ते नितोदं कुर्यान्नितोदात् प्राचीनं पुरुषान्ते नितोदयोर्नानान्तावालिखेत्तत्संनमनम्
25.6.m: Having fixed a puruṣa at the wing junction, one should make a mark on the line at the end of the puruṣa; from that mark eastward, at the end of a puruṣa, one should draw the varied ends to the two marks: that is the bending [of the wing].
By this the left wing is explained.

25.6.s: dvipuruṣaṃ paścādardhapuruṣaṃ purastāccaturbhāgonaḥ puruṣa āyāmo'ṣṭādaśa karaṇyau pārśvayostāḥ pañcadaśa parigṛhṇanti tatpuccham
25.6.d: द्विपुरुषं पश्चादर्धपुरुषं पुरस्ताच्चतुर्भागोनः पुरुष आयामोऽष्टादश करण्यौ पार्श्वयोस्ताः पञ्चदश परिगृह्णन्ति तत्पुच्छम्
25.6.m: Two puruṣas at the back, half a puruṣa in front, less by a fourth part of a puruṣa in length; eighteen are the producing sides of the flanks; they enclose fifteen: that is the tail.
One should construct the sixteenth-part [brick] with four [cords]:
by one-eighth, by three-eighths, by one-fourth, and by one-fourth without excess.
by two fourths, and by a fourth with the excess.
one side by a fourth, and two sides by a fourth with the excess.
The wing-brick with four [cords]:
by two fourths, and by two sevenths.
The wing-middle brick with four [cords]:
by two fourths, and by two times two-sevenths.
one side by a fourth, one side by a fourth and a seventh, and by a fourth with the excess and a seventh.

25.6.s: pakṣakaraṇyāḥ saptamaṃ tiryaṅmānī puruṣacaturthaṃ ca pārśvamānī tasyākṣṇayārajjvā karaṇaṃ prajṛmbhayet
25.6.d: पक्षकरण्याः सप्तमं तिर्यङ्मानी पुरुषचतुर्थं च पार्श्वमानी तस्याक्ष्णयारज्ज्वा करणं प्रजृम्भयेत्
25.6.m: The transverse measure is one-seventh of the wing's producing side, and the lateral measure is one-fourth of a puruṣa; with its diagonal cord, one should expand the shape.
With one-seventh of the wing-curving [measure], one should bend the boards.
In the placement: four quarter-bricks in front, in the head;
to the west of the head-junction, five;
to the east of the two wing junctions, eleven to the west;
at the tail-junction, five; to the west, five;
four wing-tip bricks at each of the two wing tips;
and crossing over at the two wing junctions.
In the body, one should place around as appropriate four sixteenth-part [bricks] each;
four wing-middle bricks each;
in the middle of both wings, one should cover the two wings with wing-bricks facing east;
the remainder one should cover with sixteenth-part [bricks].

25.6.s: aparasminprastāre purastācchirasi dve ṣoḍaśyau bāhyaviśeṣa upadadhyāt
25.6.d: अपरस्मिन्प्रस्तारे पुरस्ताच्छिरसि द्वे षोडश्यौ बाह्यविशेष उपदध्यात्
25.6.m: In the other layer, one should place two sixteenth-part [bricks] with the excess outward in front, in the head;
to the west of them, two crossing over, with the excess inward;
one should place around as appropriate with two half-bricks;
one should enclose with two [bricks] having the excess outward;
at the joints of the producing sides of the body, one should place sixteenth-part [bricks] with the excess outward;
four half-bricks at each of the two wing tips;
one should cover the two wings with wing-bricks facing north;
three half-bricks on each of the two sides of the tail;
the remainder one should cover with sixteenth-part [bricks].
The outermost are with the excess outward, except for the tail.

25.6.s: yaccaturaśraṃ tryaśri vā saṃpadyetārdheṣṭakābhiḥ pādeṣṭakābhirvā tatpracchādayet
25.6.d: यच्चतुरश्रं त्र्यश्रि वा संपद्येतार्धेष्टकाभिः पादेष्टकाभिर्वा तत्प्रच्छादयेत्
25.6.m: Whatever square or triangular space results, one should cover it with half-bricks or quarter-bricks.
Smaller bricks take the place of the fifteenth-part [bricks].
The heron-shaped altar and the alaja-bird-shaped altar are explained by the falcon-shaped altar.

25.6.s: evamiva śyenasya varṣīyādgasau pakṣau pucchādvakrau saṃnataṃ pucche dīrgha ātmā'maṇḍalaḥ śiraśca
25.6.d: एवमिव श्येनस्य वर्षीयाद्गसौ पक्षौ पुच्छाद्वक्रौ संनतं पुच्छे दीर्घ आत्माऽमण्डलः शिरश्च

25.6.m: Because of the force of the sacred text.

25.6.s: vijñāyate ca kaṅkacitam̐ śīrṣaṇvantaṃ cinvīta yaḥ kāmayeta saśīrṣā'muṣmim̐lloke saṃbhaveyamiti vidyamāne kathaṃ brūyāt
25.6.d: विज्ञायते च कङ्कचितँ शीर्षण्वन्तं चिन्वीत यः कामयेत सशीर्षाऽमुष्मिँल्लोके संभवेयमिति विद्यमाने कथं ब्रूयात्
25.6.m: And it is known [from scripture]: “He who desires, ‘May I be born with a head in the yonder world,’ should pile [the fire-altar] shaped like a heron with a head.” Since this [text] exists, how could one say [it is headless]?

25.6.s: prākṛtau vakrau pakṣau saṃnataṃ pucche vikāraśravaṇāt
25.6.d: प्राकृतौ वक्रौ पक्षौ संनतं पुच्छे विकारश्रवणात्

25.6.m: The body is according to the archetype, because there is no modification.
As to what is said: 'One should construct the falcon-shaped altar,' that is explained to the extent of its correspondence with scripture.
'The altar becomes threefold' is known for the horse sacrifice; there, repetition of all occurs, because there is no specific distinction.
The combination of the wings and the tail has been stated by the combination of rectangles.
It is known [from scripture] that at the horse sacrifice the fire-altar becomes twenty-one-fold.
In that case, there is repetition of the man's height, not of the cubits and spans, because of the connection with number, because of the connection with number.
